statement.p: (b) Find the best linear approximation of g(x,y) for (x,y) near (5,4).
(c) Use the approximation in part (b) to estimate g(5.03, 4.02).

static.solution:
(a) We have g_x = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+2y+16}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_x(5, 4) = \frac{5}{7} and g_y = \frac{2}{2 \sqrt{x^{2}+2y+16}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_y(5, 4) = \frac{1}{7}. Thus \nabla g(5,4) = \frac{5}{7}\, \vec i + \frac{1}{7}\, \vec j.
(b) Using the value g(5, 4) = 7 and the partial derivatives in part (a) we have g(x, y) = \sqrt{x^{2}+2y+16} \approx 7 + \frac{5}{7} (x-5) + \frac{1}{7} (y-4).
(c) Using the linearization in part (b), we have g(5.03, 4.02) \approx 7 + \frac{5}{7} (5 - 5.03) + \frac{1}{7} (4 - 4.02) = 7.02429.
